description: MY SIRR simulates soil moisture and crop dynamics to compare irrigation strategies. Its contributors publish Python code with a graphical interface and input examples. The user supplies climate forcing, soil properties, crop settings and an irrigation plan; the outputs support comparisons of water stress, crop outcomes and irrigation use. The spatial scale is the agricultural enterprise represented by those inputs. The weather sequence defines the modelled period and temporal step, so the software has no fixed geographic or historical coverage. It can support simulation of agricultural water demand and adaptation to dry conditions. The GitHub source is public and free under GPL-3.0. The own README describes Python 2.7, which may complicate use on current systems. Results depend on the chosen soil and crop parameters and on the forcing data. No related catalogue record was identified. This review checked metadata and documentation only; it did not run a crop scenario.
